styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small cast-iron prop with 15 distinct colours, all inside about one tile. That matches or beats the references on colour count (hedge 11, bench 14, lamp 14) and per-tile density (hedge 10, cheese stall 17, well 20). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no dead 5x5 blocks. By eye it shows roughly 5 grey steps, with a lighter top and edge highlights against darker body and base. The outline is 100% near-neutral, which strictly reads as near_black. But the material is grey iron, and the iron lamp-crook reference measures the same 100% neutral. Its dark edge is therefore the dark end of the iron ramp, not a uniform black sticker line. Outlines are not applied to every shape; value steps separate the forms. Texture is modest because the piece is tiny, but the shading and density hold up next to the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey cast-iron stand. Its 15 colours per tile are at or above the lamp-crook and bench references (14 distinct colours each), and its 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, so it is not flat-filled. The weak points are the outline and the shading. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so it has a uniform black/grey outline with no tint toward the adjacent material. Beodeul's richer props (cheese stall 1%, hedge 0%, well 33%) use tinted dark edges. Only the iron lamp-crook is also fully neutral, and the iron material gives that one some excuse. The candidate reads as a dark-outlined sticker around a grey body with a pale top. It has about 4 lightness steps against roughly 5-6 on the references, and little per-part grain or highlight work beyond a few speckles. Because the outline reads as near-black, and when in doubt the rule is to fail, it fails.

Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat areas. By eye it shows roughly 5 grey steps, with a light top plate, mid body, dark underside and small highlight dots on the metal, which is comparable to the iron lamp-crook reference. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny grey iron prop. By the numbers it holds up: 15 colours per tile against a reference median of 10-20, 0% flat-fill coverage, and 15 distinct colours against 11-40 for the references. The problem is the outline and shading. 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so it reads as a colourless dark line around the whole silhouette. That is the sticker look, set against references whose outlines mostly lean toward the material tone (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33%, bench 44% neutral). Only the iron lamp-crook is equally neutral. Because the iron body is also grey, the object has only about 4 grey steps and little interior grain, and it is much less rich than the roofed well or the cheese stall. The distinct-colour count is only comparable to the thin lamp and bench, so it looks thinner and flatter than the richer references. I could not clearly justify a pass on a piece with a uniform neutral outline and a shallow ramp, so the verdict is fail.
